To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
power is a relational construct, and as such, it is not only about having or using power but also about how others respond to power and how power is construed by the power holder.
Power is an essential part of social life and influences how people communicate.

(i) power is a multidimensional concept that can be construed and exercised as responsibility or opportunity; (ii) language use in social contexts shapes how power is construed, and (iii) power is used to responsible ends when it is construed as opportunity and to exploitative ends when it is used as responsibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how social context and language shape the construal and exercise of social power.
the interplay between power and language and communication.
how language and communication shape and are shaped by power in social context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
power and language are closely intertwined and that they mutually shape each other.
power is an ambiguous construct that is both a means to an end (e.g. to achieve a goal) as well as an end in itself (i.e. the goal).
the way in which power is construed is crucial for the way it is exercised.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social context shapes how power is construed, and this in turn shapes the use and effects of power.
power is a social construction, which is created and maintained through communication.
power is a social construction and a social resource, and that language is a key means of power.
The main takeaway from our work is that
power is a social construct that is not only shaped by the social context, but also serves to shape it.
power can be construed as either a resource or a burden, and this construal shapes how power is enacted in the communication process.
power can be understood in terms of opportunities and responsibilities and how these are construed, and that language and communication can be used to influence the way in which power is construed.
